A is marked with 20°, indicating ∠A = 20°. Point D is on AC, and BD is connected; the two arc marks at B show that BD bisects ∠ABC. Reasoning: In triangle ABC, ∠A + ∠B + ∠C = 180°. It is known that ∠A = 20° and ∠C = 90°, so ∠ABC = 180° - 20° - 90° = 70°. Because BD is the angle bisector of ∠ABC, ∠DBC = 70° ÷ 2 = 35°. In triangle BDC, DC is on AC, and AC ⟂ BC, so ∠BCD = 90°. Therefore ∠BDC = 180° - 90° - 35° = 55°.

method.method_draft: Image: the diagram shows triangle ABC with A on the left, C on the lower right, B above C, a right-angle mark at C, point D on AC, and BD drawn as the bisector of the angle at B. Text: ∠A = 20° and BD bisects ∠ABC. Reasoning: since ∠C = 90° and ∠A = 20°, triangle angle sum gives ∠ABC = 180° - 90° - 20° = 70°. Because BD bisects ∠ABC, ∠DBC = 35°. Now in triangle BDC, ∠BCD = 90° because DC lies on AC and AC ⟂ BC. So ∠BDC = 180° - 90° - 35° = 55°.
